practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient and reuse it for the whole process (singleton client) rather than creating/closing a client per request or per item.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single MongoClient instance per process: create the MongoClient once at application start (with the DOCUMENTDB_URI from env) and share it across modules; do not open/close a new client per request or per job item.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on connections and never disable certificate verification in production (ensure tls=true and a valid CA store).
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL on the connection string and verify certificates (use the SRV or standard connection string setting that enforces tls=true / ssl=true); never connect without TLS to the DocumentDB endpoint.

practices.practice: Disable retryable-writes in the connection string / client (e.g., retryWrites=false) because Azure DocumentDB's deployment guidance warns against leaving retryable-writes on by default.

practices.practice: Tune MongoDB driver pool options to the deployment context (small maxPoolSize/minPoolSize for serverless; larger pools and minPoolSize for long-running OLTP servers) rather than one-size-fits-all defaults.
In serverless or function environments initialize the client outside the handler so warm invocations reuse the same MongoClient instance (avoid per-invocation connect/close).
Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) so the index serves the query and avoids an in-memory blocking sort.

Create a compound index on the fields used by the abandoned-cart query (for example { status: 1, lastUpdated: 1 } with ESR ordering) so the pipeline's filter (status + timestamp range) is covered and efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Index the timestamp used for 'abandoned' queries (e.g., abandonedAt or lastUpdated) and the status field as a compound index such as { status: 1, abandonedAt: 1 } so the pipeline query (status='abandoned' and abandonedAt < now - 2h) is covered and efficient.

practices.practice: Use a partial or sparse index for the abandoned condition (e.g., createIndex({ lastUpdated: 1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { status: 'abandoned' } })) when only a subset of documents are 'abandoned' to save index size and RU costs.
practices.prior_belief: Create a partial or sparse index if many carts are active but only a subset are 'abandoned' (e.g., createIndex({ abandonedAt: 1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { status: 'abandoned' } })) to reduce index size and RU costs.

practices.practice: Project only the fields the pipeline needs (e.g., _id, customerId, contact preference, items, lastUpdated) to reduce network transfer and RU consumption.
practices.prior_belief: Project only the fields needed by the pipeline (e.g., _id, customerId, contactPreference, items, abandonedAt) instead of fetching whole documents to reduce network and RU consumption.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (e.g., 429, transient network errors) and make operations idempotent where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use retry with exponential backoff for transient network/timeout/server-selection errors and make operations idempotent (e.g., for send + log steps retry log writes and avoid double-sends by recording a send-intent flag first).

practices.practice: Run explain("executionStats") on the abandoned-cart query before scaling up the pipeline to confirm the chosen index is used and to measure RU/doc ratios.
practices.prior_belief: Before running the pipeline at scale, run explain() on the main abandoned-cart query to confirm the chosen index is used and that RU consumption is acceptable; adjust indexes or query shape accordingly.

practices.practice: Use a TTL index (createIndex({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: <seconds> })) to automatically remove stale carts or short-lived logs when appropriate, but verify retention meets auditing needs.
practices.prior_belief: Use a TTL index if you want automatic cleanup of stale carts or logs (createIndex({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: <seconds> })) but ensure the TTL interval and retention policy are suitable for audit/logging needs.

practices.practice: Choose a partition (shard) key with your access patterns in mind—keep related documents that require transactional locality together (e.g., customerId for cart+logs) and avoid hot keys; default to single-shard unless the collection's size/throughput justifies sharding.
practices.prior_belief: Design the partitioning (shard/partition key) so that frequently-updated related documents (cart + outcome logs) share the same partition key (for example customerId) if you need transactional updates or efficient multi-document locality.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs (route to Log Analytics) and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation so you can find and fix expensive queries.
Pick storage and compute separately: prefer Premium SSD v2 for new clusters and size compute tier for IOPS/bandwidth (IOPS are gated by compute tier, not disk size).

For local development use the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (Mongo protocol on port 10260), drive connection config from env vars, and only relax TLS certificate validation in dev via env-driven flags (do not default tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true in code).
Create indexes before bulk-importing seed data and await index creation (do not assume instant availability) so verification runs don't do expensive collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes before bulk-importing seed data and await index creation; do not assume instant index availability — build or ensure indexes in the seed script (createIndex and await) to avoid expensive collection scans during verification runs.

practices.practice: Keep connection URIs and provider credentials out of source control and prefer Azure Key Vault or Key Vault references for passwords and secrets; never embed API keys in documents.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the connection URI/credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment variables and recommend storing secrets in Azure Key Vault (or another secret store); never commit credentials into repo or seed files.

practices.practice: For vector search pick the index type by scale (vector-ivf under ~10k, vector-hnsw up to ~50k, vector-diskann for 500k+ vectors) and tune the engine-specific parameters (numLists, M / efConstruction / lBuild / maxDegree) appropriately.
Normalize and store fixed-dimension numeric embeddings (and record model name and dimension) and choose the vector similarity metric (COS/L2/IP) that matches your query-time normalization.

practices.practice: Create vector indexes with explicit parameters (kind, dimensions, similarity, lBuild/maxDegree) before bulk-ingesting vectors so index build/insert performance and recall are predictable.
practices.prior_belief: Create vector indexes with explicit parameters before ingesting vectors (specify index type: HNSW/IVF, and parameters like M, efConstruction for HNSW or nlist for IVF) to ensure insert/query performance is predictable.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC and Key Vault references for cluster admin credentials over long-lived passwords; create least-privilege service accounts for applications.
Restrict network access with firewall rules or Private Endpoints and avoid leaving public access open (do not allow 0.0.0.0/0 except during short tests).

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit and avoid embedding large blobs directly in documents (store large binary data in blob storage and reference it from the document).
practices.prior_belief: Limit document size and avoid embedding huge blobs (keep docs well under 16MB); if you must store large binary or large collections, use GridFS or external blob storage and reference the blob from the document.

practices.practice: Use upsert operations for seed scripts and design outcome writes to be idempotent (use updateOne/replaceOne with upsert: true or deterministic unique keys) so re-running seeds and retries are safe.

practices.practice: When you need atomicity across multiple documents, use client sessions and multi-document transactions (startSession()/withTransaction()) and prefer keeping transactional documents in the same logical partition to avoid cross-shard costs.

practices.practice: Avoid scanning the entire collection each run: use an indexed filter, a cursor with pagination or batch limits, and process results in manageable chunks rather than loading all matches into memory.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid scanning the entire carts collection each run; instead run a targeted query with indexed fields (status and abandonedAt range) and apply a reasonable batch size/limit; use a cursor and pagination to process results in manageable chunks.

practices.practice: Store only minimal contact metadata (contact method and handle) in operational documents and keep sensitive PII encrypted or in a restricted store; avoid putting external provider credentials into documents.

practices.practice: Monitor RU consumption and provision throughput appropriately (test realistic workloads, watch consumed RUs, and use autoscale or increase throughput for bulk operations such as indexing or seed imports).

practices.practice: Use explain() and server-side slow-query logs / profiling regularly to capture slow queries and high RU usage and include query plan captures in performance checks.
